desc:
Given an array nums of positive integers and an integer k, count the pairs of indices i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] is divisible by k.

nums = [30, 20, 150, 100, 40], k = 60
matching pairs: (30, 150), (20, 100), (20, 40)
result = 3
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer
hints: Checking every pair is O(n2). Only the remainders modulo k matter, not the values themselves.
a + b is divisible by k exactly when a % k and b % k add up to 0 or to k. So the partner remainder of r is (k - r) % k.
Scan left to right with a counter of remainders seen so far. For each element add count[(k - r) % k] to the answer, then record r.
editorial: Replace every number by its remainder r = x % k. A pair is good when the remainders sum to a multiple of k, which means r1 + r2 = 0 (both zero) or r1 + r2 = k. Equivalently, the partner of remainder r is (k - r) % k.

Walk through the array keeping a counter (an array of size k) of earlier remainders. For the current element, every earlier element with the partner remainder forms one new pair; add that count and then record the current remainder. Because each pair is counted when its later element arrives, no pair is counted twice and a number is never paired with itself. This runs in O(n + k) time and O(k) space.
solution:
def countPairs(nums, k):
    cnt = [0] * k
    total = 0
    for x in nums:
        r = x % k
        total += cnt[(k - r) % k]
        cnt[r] += 1
    return total
